items.title: CVE-2026-60004: Gitea Gitea Code Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Review Gitea deployments for CVE-2026-60004 exposure where untrusted users possess repository write access.
items.summary: Gitea contains a code injection vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-60004 that allows an attacker with repository write access to send a malicious patch to the diffpatch API endpoint. This enables them to plant an executable Git hook and run shell commands as the Gitea service account. CISA has added the flaw to its KEV catalog with a federal remediation deadline of August 28, 2026. Organizations must apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use of the product.

items.bottom_line: Gitea instances are vulnerable to remote code execution via the diffpatch API endpoint if users have repository write access.

items.title: Carhartt data breach exposes information of 12.9 million accounts
items.one_liner: Monitor cloud analytics platforms like Databricks for credential theft and unauthorized data exfiltration similar to the Carhartt incident.
items.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion group published sensitive data stolen from clothing retailer Carhartt after the company refused a $3.3 million ransom demand. The breach, which compromised Carhartt's Databricks analytics platform, exposed over 50GB of documents affecting more than 12.9 million accounts and containing customer emails, names, phone numbers, addresses, and internal corporate data. Have I Been Pwned founder Troy Hunt verified the scale of the leak, which also included over 15,000 employee records with corporate email addresses.
items.bottom_line: Carhartt suffered a massive data breach affecting nearly 13 million accounts after refusing a $3.3 million ransom from ShinyHunters.

items.title: CVE-2026-5388 (CRITICAL 9.3): justhtml before 1.15.0 contains multiple security issues in URL sanitization helpers (clean_url_value/clean_u…
items.one_liner: Upgrade justhtml to version 1.15.0 or later to fix critical URL sanitization and script injection flaws.
items.summary: The justhtml package before version 1.15.0 has been found to contain multiple security issues in URL sanitization helpers, HTML serialization, and Markdown passthrough features, assigned CVE-2026-5388 with a critical CVSS score of 9.3. Depending on the configuration, attackers can bypass sanitization to inject active HTML and JavaScript through encoded javascript URLs, backslash-based relative URLs, or raw element reintroduction. Most custom-policy issues primarily affect helper APIs, programmatic DOM construction, and custom transformation pipelines rather than default sanitize configurations.
items.bottom_line: Applications using justhtml helper APIs or custom policies prior to 1.15.0 are vulnerable to critical HTML and JavaScript injection.

Public rhetoric between officials from both nations has intensified significantly, threatening deeply integrated cross-border supply chains.

items.title: Disrupting supply chain attacks on npm and GitHub Actions
items.one_liner: GitHub strengthens npm and Actions defaults with account lockouts and safer fork checkouts to stop supply chain attacks.
items.summary: GitHub has implemented several product security improvements across npm and GitHub Actions to disrupt common supply chain attack techniques used to spread malware. New preventive measures include placing high-impact npm accounts into a 72-hour read-only mode when email addresses or 2FA recovery codes are changed. For GitHub Actions, GitHub changed the default behavior of actions/checkout to prevent checking out untrusted code from forks during vulnerable triggers, and introduced granular workflow execution policies for enterprises and organizations. These combined technical constraints and policy controls are designed to break initial compromise vectors often leveraged in malicious open-source campaigns.

items.bottom_line: New default controls on npm and GitHub Actions significantly restrict account takeover and untrusted fork code execution.

items.one_liner: NVIDIA TensorRT ONNX file parsing flaw allows remote code execution via malformed Slice operations.
items.summary: NVIDIA TensorRT contains an improper validation flaw within the parsing of Slice operations in ONNX models, leading to a write past the end of an allocated array. Successful exploitation enables execution of arbitrary code in the context of the current TensorRT process, prompting NVIDIA to release security updates.

items.title: CVE-2026-78183 (CRITICAL 9.8): DBD::Pg version 3.21.0 for Perl has a heap out-of-bounds write in quote_float. quote_float() allocates the le…
items.one_liner: Patch or downgrade Perl's DBD::Pg module away from version 3.21.0 to eliminate the heap out-of-bounds write.
items.summary: DBD::Pg version 3.21.0 for Perl contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the quote_float function, tracked as CVE-2026-78183 with a critical CVSS score of 9.8. The function allocates the length of the string plus one byte for bare numeric symbols, but for special literals like Infinity and NaN, it emits the literal surrounded by quotes plus a null byte, which overflows by two bytes. This regression was introduced during the quote.c rewrite and can be triggered via methods like $dbh->quote.

items.title: Activating Latent Security Knowledge through LLM-Guided Risk Analysis for Secure Code Generation
items.one_liner: BRACE improves LLM-generated code security without retraining by using an expert LLM to inject task-specific risk cues during inference.
items.summary: BRACE is an inference-time, training-free security harness designed to improve secure code generation by activating latent security knowledge in LLMs. Instead of fine-tuning, the framework uses an LLM to identify task-relevant security risks and provides these as cues to the code-generating model. This approach significantly increases the safe code rate, raising it from 33.9% to 91.2% on the CyberNative benchmark.
items.bottom_line: Insecure code generation is often a failure to activate existing knowledge rather than a knowledge deficit, and can be corrected via inference-time risk-conditioned prompting.

items.title: LLMscope: Extracting LLM Assets from Edge AI Chips via Optical Probing
items.one_liner: Optical probing and laser voltage imaging can extract sensitive LLM weights and activations from edge AI accelerators during inference.
items.summary: LLMscope demonstrates that physical side-channel attacks via laser voltage imaging can extract LLM operational assets, such as embeddings, attention weights, and quantized MLP activations, from edge AI chips during inference. By attacking an FPGA-based accelerator that reuses memory buffers and compute subcircuits across layers, the researchers achieved full recovery of targeted values. The work establishes mathematical lower bounds proving that direct asset recovery scales linearly with asset size.
items.bottom_line: Edge AI chip execution is vulnerable to laser voltage imaging, exposing proprietary model weights and activations via side-channels.

claims.text: To validate our claims, we perform an attack on an FPGA-based LLM accelerator.

items.one_liner: Linux kernel route4_set_fastmap use-after-free vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges to kernel context.
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability has been discovered in the Linux kernel net subsystem packet classifier, specifically within the route4_set_fastmap function. The flaw stems from a lack of validation regarding the existence of an object before performing operations on it. A local attacker with low-privileged code execution capabilities can exploit this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code within the context of the kernel. Linux has released patches addressing the issue under commit 47d7f7051253bdc02b1d245d87e38f16d31a74df.

items.summary: The exceljs-hardened package in versions before 5.0.0 fails to neutralize leading dangerous characters such as equals (=), plus (+), minus (-), or at (@) signs in cell values when they are exported to CSV format. items.title: Your secrets are leaking to AI coding agents (and how to stop it)
items.one_liner: AI coding agents inadvertently leak local credentials and environment secrets into third-party prompt logs, creating severe supply-chain risks.
items.summary: AI coding assistants and autonomous agents naturally absorb sensitive data like source files, configuration settings, environment variables, and terminal errors into their prompts, transmitting them to external model providers and gateway logs. This persistent context exposure bypasses traditional Git-based secret management, leaving credentials scattered across third-party systems where they can linger indefinitely. Malicious actors have begun targeting agent session histories and local environment files, as seen in supply chain attacks like Mini Shai-Hulud that harvest AWS, SSH, and npm credentials. Developers must adopt automated secret detection before data leaves the local prompt context to mitigate multi-month remediation windows.
items.bottom_line: Relying on AI coding assistants without strict secret-scanning at the prompt boundary exposes critical API keys and environment variables to third-party logs.

claims.text: AI coding agents prove useful in a number of ways, among them: they read everything.

items.one_liner: P. Chidambaram and legal think-tanks push back against the 'One Nation, One Election' Bills, exposing deep constitutional and administrative divisions in India.
items.summary: Former Union Minister P. Appearing alongside Padma awardees and various think-tanks, critics and supporters debated the merits of synchronised elections, with some highlighting administrative and developmental efficiency while others warned of potential chaos and governance vacuums.
